elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 10.5: "This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York ... without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws."

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over the merits of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, which preserves the exclusive merits forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not a defect: the preferred level is satisfied instead.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is New York County courts, not Delaware/California/London. Not a defect given the preferred level is met.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the retained New York governing-law sentence satisfies element 1, and the single inserted sentence supplies exclusive New York County merits jurisdiction with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out, satisfying element 2.

Minimal: the original governing-law sentence is left verbatim (no cosmetic deletions or paraphrase), and the insertion is one concise sentence supplying the missing forum with no extras (no fee-shifting, jury waiver, service-of-process, survival or arbitration language).

Preserves intent: no cross-references, defined terms, timing, or remedies are disturbed; the injunctive-relief carve-out does not contradict any retained sentence, and there is no competing arbitration or venue provision in the document to conflict with.

Finding status of 'deviation' is defensible because the document as drafted fixed no forum, leaving the venue element of both checklists unmet on a material term; the redline cures it at the preferred position.
